details: A conservative optimal online learner yields stable compression from its mistake examples.
proof: Use a conservative online learner with mistake bound $\mathrm L(\mathcal H)$, such as the standard optimal algorithm, and cycle it through a realizable sample until a full pass is mistake-free.  Retain only the examples on which it made a mistake.  There are at most $\mathrm L(\mathcal H)$; their labels are recoverable from the learner's successive mistaken predictions, and removing any unretained example leaves the final predictor unchanged.  This gives a stable unlabeled compression scheme of that size.
witness_verification: For the half-interval class $\mathcal I_n$, $\mathrm L=\Theta(\log n)$, while retaining the largest positive sample point (or nothing for an all-negative sample) is a stable unlabeled compression scheme of size one.  Hence the gap is unbounded.
name: Littlestone Dimension / Stable Unlabeled Complexity
